About Us

Who we are

Established in 2007, the Korean Canadian Athletic Association (KCAA) is a non-profit organization dedicated to fostering a healthy and vibrant community through sport. Serving the Greater Toronto Area, we provide a variety of sports programs for youth and adults, promoting teamwork, discipline, and leadership.

We aim to inspire future generations to thrive by instilling the confidence, values, and skills gained through sports. Lessons like perseverance, respect, and collaboration are not only essential for success on the field but also in life.

Join us as we promote active living, lifelong friendships, and a stronger, more united GTA community.

Teamwork Discipline Leadership Perseverance Respect Collaboration

Our Programs

What we run

Across hockey, basketball, and baseball, our programs serve kids and adults throughout the GTA — from a first time on the ice to competitive league play.

Hockey

Learn-to-skate through elite development

  • Future Stars Hockey Program — learn-to-skate and hockey development pathways for youth, running across multiple seasons.
  • Junior Tigers Elite — an elite development program for committed young players working toward the Junior Tigers travel team, with weekly development skates and tournament play.
  • Men's League — an adult recreational hockey league open to players of all skill levels.

Basketball

Dream Big Youth Basketball

  • A youth basketball program run in partnership with TKT Basketball.

Baseball

Youth Baseball Camp

  • Seasonal baseball programming for youth players.

Get Involved

Volunteer with KCAA

Our board and day-to-day operations run on volunteers, and our programs are led by hired, qualified coaches — that's how we make sure the families and players who register get consistent, quality coaching every season. Around that core, there's a lot of room to get involved: registration, event-day support, social media, and program development all run on volunteer hours. We're looking to grow that side, and we're a great fit for students who want real, hands-on experience.

Real experienceHands-on roles with real responsibility, not just handing out water bottles.
Flexible hoursA few hours a week or per event, on your schedule.
Community hoursMany roles can count toward school volunteer-hour requirements.
ReferencesHappy to write one for volunteers who stick around and put in the time.
NetworkingMeet coaches, board members, and other community organizations along the way.
Give backBe part of a program that's directly building a healthier, more connected community across the GTA.
Social Media / Comms

Tell our story

Run our Instagram and Facebook, capture photos and short videos at events, and help our programs get noticed.

Good fit for: marketing, communications, or media students who want real portfolio work.

Biz Mgmt / Admin

Keep things running

Help with registration, basic bookkeeping, sponsor outreach, and day-to-day board support.

Good fit for: business, commerce, or accounting students who want real nonprofit operations experience.

Skate / Hockey Program

Be on the ice

Assist our Learn-to-Skate and youth hockey sessions — teaching, supervising, and supporting our coaches.

Good fit for: anyone with skating or hockey experience, or kinesiology/sport science students.

Sport Program Development

Help us grow

Plan basketball and baseball events, scout new sports like pickleball, and shape how our programs run.

Good fit for: sport management students, or anyone who likes building things from scratch.
